edits.new:
### 12. Contract

Rule-model read (GAP-0722): GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{version} answers packageCode, versionLabel, checksum (SHA-256), model content, compiler version and valid-from date. Property types, lengths and required flags stay open with the rwb-decision owner; the WireMock fake carries these element names as assumed shapes.

Rule-catalog read (GAP-2405, GAP-0722): GET /rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion= answers 200 with packageCode, packageVersion, versionState, inForce, ruleId, ruleVersion, actionText, ownerRole, timerSpec, toState, droolsRuleName and outputs. An unknown rule or version answers 404 with MSG-P3-027; a malformed packageVersion parameter answers 422 with MSG-GEN-001.

**Registry scope.** The four rule registry tables (rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row, rule_test_case) are owned by rwb-decision in its own schema, and this story builds no P3 or P4 declaration of them (GAP-1301). The registry, the seeding, the admin operations, the approval, the rollback and JOB-20 stay in RWB-P7-E2042-APP (ASM-A6-tables-3). This story keeps the workbook authoring, the Blob object, the model cache, the checksum check, the atomic swap, the catalog read and the schema assertion, and proves AC1 to AC3 against the rwb-decision contract mock here; the real-service proof is in RWB-ITG-E2042-ITG (GAP-0721).

**Pattern application**
